Eva believes that trying new things keeps life fresh. On Monday evenings, Eva reviews the notes from class. Eva has practiced chess for three years and won a prize last term. Also, the old train runs on coal.
Little by little, things began to change. The river bank has become an important part of daily life. The experience taught Eva more than any book could. In fact, pigeons crowd the city square.

The plant garden looked quieter than usual that evening. David advised Eva to try dancing as a new hobby. David always says that small steps matter more than big plans. A deer fence guards the orchard.
Eva thanked David for the honest advice. Eva will take part in a chess match in January. Eva wrote down every idea in a small notebook. For example, the storm reshaped the sandy shoreline.
They talked about everything from schoolwork to future dreams. Sometimes a short talk can solve a big problem. At first, Eva found it difficult to keep the habit.
